facts.text: **Naming finding.** No published external standard is called the "14-pass review methodology." A web search for the exact phrase returns only Grant & Booth (2009), "A typology of reviews: an analysis of **14 review types**" (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19490148/). That paper classifies kinds of literature review. It is not a multipass critique method, so it is a name collision. The concept in this tree is the local `document-critique` method, "passes 0–14" (~/.claude/skills/deep-optimizer/SKILL.md). Its canonical text is ~/.claude/skills/writing-expert/r

**Summary:** No external standard, paper, or official document names a "14-pass review methodology." The only primary source is a local skill, `document-critique`. It numbers its passes 0–14. Its structure does resemble older published review methods, but the skill does not cite any of them, so that link is inference.

- **In scope:** the method itself. It is a fixed, ordered set of review passes (numbered 0–14 in the local document-critique skill). Each pass reads the whole document for one class of concern. The passes run inside a find → fix → re-review loop that repeats until a round turns up no Medium+ findings. - **Out of scope:** sibling optimizers (code, prompt, skill, SQL), the Document Critique parent domain, and general editing craft. - **No external standard exists.** No published standard, paper, or style guide defines a "14-pass review methodology" (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19490148/). 16. Formal multi-phase review of development documents goes back at least to M. E. Fagan's inspection method. It appeared in *IBM Systems Journal* 15(3):182–211 in 1976. — https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1147/sj.153.0182 17. A Fagan inspection has six named operations: planning, overview, preparation, inspection meeting, rework, and follow-up. It applies to specifications and requirements as well as code. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagan_inspection 18. Fagan's rework and follow-up steps, where a moderator checks every correction, are an early form of the "fix, then re-verify" step in document-c

- **Concept:** 14-pass review methodology (parent: Document Critique) - **Run:** /rabbithole, mechanism brief, 2026-09-24 - **Verdict:** BUDGET_EXHAUSTED (3 deepening passes; a 4th pass would likely still add evidence on pass-level efficacy, see "Unresolved")

**Evidence base.** The mechanism is tested indirectly. No source validates a 14-pass count directly. The evidence comes from two groups of studies: - human studies of scenario-based and perspective-based reading, where each reviewer or pass takes one defect focus; - LLM studies of multi-round review and self-critique, where the reviewer is a model looping over its own output.

In the original experiment (Porter, Votta & Basili, 1995), reviewers who used scenarios aimed at specific defect classes found about 35% more defects than ad hoc and checklist reviewers (https://www.cs.umd.edu/~mvz/handouts/emp_pbr.pdf). 2. Verdict: **BUDGET_EXHAUSTED (soft stop)**, not saturated. The new-information rate is falling, but it has not stayed below 5% for two consecutive passes. At least one more pass would likely pay off. The best targets are: - the full texts of the Springer replications; - Fagan's 1976 inspection paper, for the origin of phased reading; - the local document-critique pass definitions, to check the 14 passes for overlap.

**In scope.** A review methodology that runs a fixed sequence of about 14 single-focus passes over one document. Each pass looks for one class of defect. The findings are then fixed, and the loop repeats until it converges (the Document Critique / DDO "passes 0–14" pattern). This report covers only the method's boundary conditions, failure modes, disagreements, and disconfirming evidence.

**Corrections to the reports** - **Stopping rules:** the loop has seven ways to stop, not just "zero Medium+ findings". The others include no progress, the same finding coming back, a rewrite that barely changed, and a round that created as many problems as it fixed. The edge-cases and practice reports described only the first. - **Stop-rule mix-up:** the "two quiet rounds in a row" rule the practice report attributes to this method is actually /rabbithole's own stopping rule. The method's clean exit needs one clean round plus a blind re-review. - **What the method cites:** the method file cit

23. Replications did not confirm the scenario-reading advantage. Fusaro, Lanubile and Visaggio (1997) found no empirical evidence that scenarios performed better. The evidence that separate lenses find more defects is therefore mixed. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1023/A:1009724120285 24. Wohlin et al. found no significant difference between user, tester and designer perspectives in detection rate, defects per hour, or defect coverage. A checklist control group of PhD students found significantly more defects per hour. So distinct lenses may overlap more than their labels suggest. https

- **Do concern-specific passes beat checklists?** Porter et al. 1995 reported +35% for scenarios over checklists (https://www.cs.umd.edu/~mvz/handouts/emp_pbr.pdf). Fusaro et al. 1997 found no scenario advantage (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1023/A:1009742216007). The 2006 replication found the advantage only when the perspectives did not overlap (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10664-006-5967-6). Not resolved. The evidence is conditional on how distinct the passes are. - **Are checklists effective?** SmartBear says checklists are the most effective way to catch common error

**How the design holds up against the evidence** (my inference) - **Well covered:** - Reviewers inventing findings: findings without a quote or anchor get downgraded. - Reviewers critiquing the conversation instead of the document: the blind re-review sees only the document. - Findings bouncing back after fixes: the stability and no-progress exits stop the loop. - **Gaps:** - The loop's stop decisions depend on severity labels, which reviewers agree on least (κ = 0.46). - The cross-model review is off by default, even though a mix of model vendors was what caught every seeded defect in one stu

13. Extra review rounds add noise. In the "More Rounds, More Noise" study (30 artifacts, 150 injected errors), single-pass review scored F1 = 0.376. Every multi-turn variant scored lower; independent re-review scored worst at F1 = 0.263. https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.16244 14. In the same study, multi-turn review raised recall by about 0.08 but produced 62% more false positives (8.5 vs 5.2). Precision fell from 0.30 to 0.20. https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.16244 15. **What the concept is** - No published standard defines a "14-pass review methodology". The only search hit is an unrelated 2009 paper classifying 14 types of literature review. - The concept is the local `document-critique` method, v5.3.0. "14" is the number of the last pass, not a count: there are 15 whole-numbered passes, 17 always-run passes, or 18 with the optional cross-model pass.

1. I found no primary source, standard, or paper that defines a "14-pass" document review. Searching the exact phrase instead returns Grant & Booth's typology of **14 review *types***, which is a different concept (literature-review genres). Anyone searching the term can confuse the two. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19490148/ 2. Grant & Booth themselves warn that review labels overlap and are applied inconsistently. This is a naming hazard for any "N-type" or "N-pass" label. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1471-1842.2009.00848.x
**In scope:** where the "14-pass" document review method comes from, how it has changed, and which primary or official sources back it up.

The skill's external-verification pass and blind re-audit follow the Huang side, but no local evaluation tests which effect applies to prose review. - **Pass count:** the concept name says "14-pass". **Limits:** - No source studies a 14-pass sequence directly. Every claim about the method is inferred from single-focus-reading studies and multi-round-LLM studies. - The SmartBear figures come from a vendor. - Two 2026 arXiv papers (claims 13–18) are single-author preprints that have not been peer reviewed.
**Handoffs to concept-family-explorer (not researched here):** capture-recapture defect estimation as a stopping rule; Fagan inspection; LLM-as-judge calibration; multi-vendor review ensembles.

**Out of scope.** Sibling review methods (Fagan inspection as a topic, perspective-based reading as a topic, editorial "levels of edit") are cited only as evidence for this concept's mechanisms. They are not researched as concepts in their own right. The parent domain, Document Critique, is also out of scope.
